transcript.text: Elena, my laboratory analysis on these drums is complete. The spent coolant was found to contain 2.4% chlorinated solvent. Under our site's waste matrix, any batch at or above 1.0% chlorinated solvent must be routed to hazardous-liquid treatment rather than ordinary coolant recycling. This result was completed yesterday but has not yet been attached to the waste authorization file. Given this finding, all fourteen drums should be designated for hazardous-liquid treatment, not the standard coolant recycling route. I'll make sure the analysis result gets formally attached to the waste authorization once we proceed.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share the logistical constraint I mentioned earlier. I confirmed with our disposal contractor that their tanker permit allows no more than 8 of these drums on a single load. This means the 14 drums must be shipped as two separate loads: one load of 8 drums and a second load of 6 drums. I received this permit condition in the contractor's service email, but I have not yet entered it into the transport booking system. We'll need to factor this into the removal plan and the scheduling of pickups.
